terms.gloss: fee, charge (for work or a service); wages, rent
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.126: quī cum mercēde docēret
terms.comment: What is paid for work or for the use of something, as pretium is what goods cost.

terms.gloss: name a price, ask so much: charge
evidence: M-O s.v. sale: ask (a certain price) for something, charge
terms.comment: With the genitive of price: quantī indicās?, how much are you asking? (Vives, cited by Morgan–Owens). Not to be confused with indīcō, indīcere, to proclaim.

terms.gloss: set a price (of a seller or a buyer)
evidence: Plaut. Pers. 4.4.37: indicā, fac pretium (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Mil. 3.1.133: pretium statuere mercī (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Indicā, fac pretium. — Tua mers est, tua indicātiōst.
phrases.english: Name your price. — They’re your goods; the pricing is yours.
to charge a price for, set a price on
at a high (low, very low, exorbitant) price

phrases.latin: Pretium eī in lībrās est decem dēnāriīs.
phrases.english: The price for it is ten denarii a pound.

sources: Lewis & Short: pretium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 130–131, 289.
Lewis & Short: merces · Lewis & Short: indico
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. sale.
